system.name: NCC
system.one_liner: a concurrency-control protocol for strictly serializable datastores that commits naturally-consistent concurrent transactions without unnecessary aborts or validation overhead

content.subject: comparing dOCC, which falsely aborts a naturally-consistent transaction, against NCC, which commits both via timestamps and a safeguard check

elements.name: A
elements.role: version timeline of key A, starting at version A0

elements.name: B
elements.role: version timeline of key B, starting at version B0

elements.name: tx1
elements.role: client 1's transaction, reads A and writes B

elements.name: tx2
elements.role: client 2's transaction, reads A and writes B

elements.name: Validate
elements.role: validation phase, where dOCC checks for conflicts and can hold locks

elements.name: Abort
elements.role: tx2 is forced to abort after failing validation

elements.name: lock icon
elements.role: B is locked by tx1 during validation, then unlocked, blocking tx2's conflicting write

relations.what: tx1 writes B (w1B), acquiring its lock
tx2 attempts to write B (w2B) but finds it locked
the lock held on B blocks tx2's validation, leading to its abort

panels.label: (a) dOCC baseline
panels.differs: tx1 (cyan) locks B during validation, so tx2's (orange) conflicting write finds B unavailable and tx2 is Aborted despite being naturally consistent

panels.label: (b) timestamp refinement examples
panels.differs: a separate set of read/write transactions with different pre-assigned timestamps shows how each access refines a version's (t_w,t_r) pair

panels.label: (c) NCC
panels.differs: re-runs the same tx1(t=4)/tx2(t=8) from (a) under NCC: pre-assignment plus a safeguard check (SG) lets both Async Commit, with no lock or abort

values.what: each version's timestamp pair (t_w, t_r) and each transaction's pre-assigned timestamp, shown numerically at every lifeline crossing
values.result_cells: cyan values belong to tx1's lineage, orange to tx2's; each panel ends in a labelled outcome (Commit/Abort in (a), refined (t_w,t_r) pairs in (b), Async Commit in (c))

content.key_idea: The same two naturally-consistent transactions that dOCC's locking validation falsely aborts under contention are both committed by NCC's timestamp pre-assignment, refinement, and safeguard check, with a middle panel showing how per-version timestamps get refined.
content.reading_order: left to right along each lifeline in (a) watching tx2 hit the lock and abort; then (b)'s refinement examples; then (c) re-running (a)'s scenario to see both transactions succeed

palette.used_for: cyan: tx1/CL1's lifeline, labels, and version values throughout all three panels
orange: tx2/CL2's lifeline, labels, and version values throughout all three panels
white fill of small annotation boxes (e.g. version-name boxes like {A0}, and the SG safeguard checkbox)

style.stroke: thin grey lifeline arrows and crossing diagonals; black for the lock icon and SG/RTC callout boxes
style.arrows: many thin crossing diagonal arrows between lifelines representing request/response messages, open arrowheads; a dashed cyan arrow in (b) tracking one version's timestamp update
style.icons: a padlock icon (locked/unlocked) on B in (a); a small 'SG' safeguard checkbox and 'RTC' callout in (c)

encoding.color_means: cyan marks everything belonging to tx1's/CL1's lineage; orange marks everything belonging to tx2's/CL2's lineage, consistently across all three panels
encoding.line_style_means: solid diagonal arrows carry request/response messages between lifelines; a dashed cyan arrow in (b) specifically tracks one version's timestamp being refined
encoding.state_means: the outcome in each panel (Commit vs Abort in (a), Async Commit in (c)) is told apart by explicit text labels rather than colour or ghosting
encoding.marker_means: a padlock icon marks a locked/unlocked key; 'SG' marks NCC's added safeguard check
encoding.emphasis: re-using the identical tx1/tx2 cyan/orange colouring and values across (a) and (c) lets the reader directly see the same scenario succeed under NCC where it failed under dOCC
reusable_patterns: swimlane timelines for two clients and the keys they touch, with per-client colour coding kept consistent across a 'before' and 'after' panel to highlight a protocol fix
weaknesses: panel (b) uses different transactions/timestamps from (a) and (c), so a reader must notice the scenario has changed before comparing it against the other two panels

evidence: NCC can commit both transactions with timestamp pre-assignment, refinement, and the safeguard check (denoted by SG).
such contention windows lead to false aborts, where a transaction is aborted despite being consistent.
dOCC incurs unnecessary validation costs, and could be falsely aborted due to lock unavailability.

summary: This three-panel figure from NCC's background section illustrates the timestamp-inversion pitfall and NCC's fix using swimlane timelines for CL1, key A, key B, and CL2. In (a), dOCC baseline, tx1 (cyan) and tx2 (orange) both read A and write B; tx1 locks B during validation, so tx2's conflicting write is blocked and tx2 is Aborted even though the two transactions are naturally consistent. Panel (b) is a separate set of examples showing how each read or write refines a version's (t_w, t_r) timestamp pair. In (c), NCC re-runs the exact same tx1/tx2 scenario from (a) but with pre-assigned timestamps, refinement, and a safeguard check (SG); both transactions now reach Async Commit, with no locking and no false abort.
summary_zh: 该图用CL1/A/B/CL2泳道时间线说明时间戳倒置问题及NCC的解法：(a)dOCC基线中tx1(蓝)在验证阶段锁住B，导致自然一致的tx2(橙)被错误Abort；(b)另举例说明每次读写如何修正版本的(t_w,t_r)时间戳对；(c)NCC用时间戳预分配、修正与安全检查(SG)重跑同一场景，两个事务均异步提交成功。
notes: Combined all three source SVGs (texfig1a_bg, texfig1b_bg_p2, texfig1c_bg_p3) to build style.palette, since the context file's given colour histogram covers all three files' fills/strokes together; grep against each file individually confirmed the same two colours (#00b0f0, #ff9300) recur in all three panels. Panel (b) illustrates a general timestamp-refinement rule with different transactions/values than (a)/(c)'s shared tx1/tx2 scenario; it is still listed as a comparison-axis panel since it is one of the figure's three lettered sub-figures, but its differing scenario is called out in its own 'differs' text rather than treated as a strict alternative outcome.
